name: Nepal Road Standard 2070 (2013), Department of Roads
version: NRS 2027 second revision 2070 (2013) - transcribed 2026-09-20 from Resource/Nepal Road Standard (NRS) 2070.pdf

meta.note: Values transcribed table by table from the printed NRS 2070 with clause / table references in each 'source'. Tables whose status is 'default' are application defaults where the standard gives no number (they are marked as such in the checks). cl. 2 b: requirements may be relaxed by the Government of Nepal in very difficult situations; cl. 7 b: the design speed may be reduced to 75 % in very difficult terrain.

class_labels.I: Class I - expressway, divided carriageway, > 20,000 PCU/day (20-year), 120 km/h in plain terrain
class_labels.II: Class II - arterial, 5,000 - 20,000 PCU/day, 100 km/h in plain terrain
class_labels.III: Class III - collector, 2,000 - 5,000 PCU/day, 80 km/h in plain terrain
class_labels.IV: Class IV - local, < 2,000 PCU/day, 60 km/h in plain terrain

meta.class_correlation: Table 3-1: National Highways are class I-II (plain / rolling) or II-III (mountainous / steep); Feeder Roads class II-III or III-IV
meta.terrain_source: Table 6-1 (percent cross slope of the country across the alignment)

design_speed.note: cl. 7 b: may be reduced to 75 % of the table value in very difficult terrain and unavoidable circumstances

eye_height.source: NRS 2070 cl. 8.3 d driver's eye height

min_radius.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-1 minimum recommended radius when no superelevation is provided (2.5 % adverse camber); also Table 24-1

min_radius_absolute.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-1 minimum radius with the maximum superelevation of 10 %

min_radius_comfort.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-1 radius from the passenger comfort criterion (lateral force 15 % of vertical), eq. 24-3 R = V^2/20

side_friction.source: NRS 2070 Table 24-4 coefficient of lateral friction

longitudinal_friction.source: NRS 2070 Table 24-2 coefficient of longitudinal friction (stopping distance)

max_superelevation.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.6 b: 7 % in plain and rolling terrain, 10 % in hilly areas not bound by snow
max_superelevation.note: 7 % in snow-bound areas (see max_superelevation_snow_bound); minimum superelevation equals the camber (cl. 11.6 c)

max_superelevation_snow_bound.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.6 b: 7 % in snow bound areas

superelevation_relative_gradient.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.6 e: outer edge not steeper than 1 in 150 (plain, rolling) or 1 in 60 (mountainous, steep) relative to the centre line

transition_required_below_radius.source: NRS 2070 cl. 9.2 b, c: all horizontal curves with radius below 1000 m are provided with clothoid transition curves

transition_shift_min.source: NRS 2070 cl. 9.2 f and eq. 24-7: no transition is needed when the shift L^2 / (24 R) is below 0.25 m

min_transition_length.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-2 Length of transition curves (by radius); footnote: applicable when L <= R x deflection (eq. 24-5)

transition_a_ratio_min.source: NRS 2070 cl. 19 d: clothoid parameter A = sqrt(R L) within 0.4 R and 1.4 R (aesthetics)

transition_a_ratio_max.source: NRS 2070 cl. 19 d: clothoid parameter A = sqrt(R L) within 0.4 R and 1.4 R (aesthetics)

transition_min_fraction_of_arc.source: NRS 2070 cl. 19 d: transition length not less than 1/4 of the circular curve length

max_straight_length.source: NRS 2070 cl. 19 g: maximum length of straight sections in plan 3-5 km

hairpin_deflection.source: PLM rule: a curve reversing the direction of travel (deflection over 120 deg) is treated as a hair-pin bend (NRS 2070 cl. 9.3)

hairpin_min_speed.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-3 Hair pin bends: minimum design speed

hairpin_min_radius.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-3 Hair pin bends: minimum radius of curvature

hairpin_min_transition.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-3 Hair pin bends: minimum length of transition curve

hairpin_max_gradient.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-3 Hair pin bends: maximum longitudinal gradient

hairpin_max_superelevation.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-3 Hair pin bends: maximum superelevation

hairpin_min_spacing.source: NRS 2070 cl. 9.3 b: at least 60 m between successive hair pin bends

extra_widening_single.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-4 Extrawidening on curves, single lane road (radius up to 20 / 20-40 / 40-60 m; nil above 60 m)

extra_widening_double.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-4 Extrawidening on curves, double lane road

extra_widening_per_lane_multi.source: NRS 2070 Table 9-4 Extrawidening on curves, multi lane road (per lane)

max_gradient.source: NRS 2070 Table 10-1 Maximum gradients (trucks 120 kg/kW, 25 km/h speed reduction)
max_gradient.note: cl. 10.1.2 a: eased by 0.5 % for each 500 m of altitude above mean sea level; cl. 10.1.2 b: eased on curves by (30 + R) / R %, at most 75 / R %, for gradients above 4 %

gradient_altitude_easing.source: NRS 2070 cl. 10.1.2 a grade compensation for altitude

grade_compensation_threshold.source: NRS 2070 cl. 10.1.2 c: grades below 4 % need no compensation

gradient_critical_length.source: NRS 2070 Table 10-2 Maximum (critical) length of gradient

min_gradient_drainage.source: NRS 2070 cl. 10.1.1 e: minimum longitudinal gradient for drainage 0.5 %

min_k_crest.source: NRS 2070 Table 10-3 Minimum K for summit curves

min_k_sag.source: NRS 2070 Table 10-4 Minimum K for valley curves

min_vertical_curve_length.source: PLM default: NRS 2070 governs vertical curves by K (L = K x A, cl. 10.4 e) and gives no separate minimum length

lanes.source: NRS 2070 Table 24-1 number of lanes (I: 4 min., II: >= 2, III: 2, IV: < 2)

lane_width.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-1 multilane pavement width per lane

carriageway_width.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-1 and Table 24-1: 3.5 m per lane; class IV single lane 3.75 m (3.0 m in difficult terrain) or 5.5 m intermediate lane
carriageway_width.note: class IV: the single-lane carriageway should have treated shoulders to a total treated width of 5.5 m (cl. 11.1 b)

shoulder_width.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-2 and Table 24-1 minimum shoulder width (reduced in mountainous and steep terrain, cl. 11.2 d)

shoulder_min_width.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.2 a: shoulders at least 0.75 m on either side

shoulder_crossfall_extra.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.5 d: shoulder crossfall 0.5 % steeper than the carriageway

camber.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-3 Camber (cement concrete 1.5-2.0, bituminous 2.5, gravel 4.0, earthen 5.0)

median_width.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.3 b: median 5 m recommended, 3 m where land is restricted

right_of_way.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-6 Right of way (total width): Highways 50, Feeder Roads 30, District Roads 20

vertical_clearance.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.9.3 e: 5.0 m over the whole roadway width

fill_slope.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-4 Embankment side slopes (1:4 below 1.5 m, 1:3 to 3.0 m, 1:2.5 to 4.5 m, 1:2 to 12 m; above 12 m designed specially)

max_fill_height.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-4: embankments higher than 12 m are designed specially

embankment_step_min_width.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.7 c: on natural cross slopes steeper than 1:5 the ground is cut in horizontal steps wider than 2 m

embankment_step_cross_slope.source: NRS 2070 cl. 11.7 c: benching under fills required above a 1:5 (20 %) cross slope

cut_slope.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-5 Cuttings side slopes, steepest of the recommended range (ordinary soil 1:2 to 1:1; disintegrated rock 1:1/2 to 1:1/4; soft rock, shale 1:1/4 to 1:1/8; medium rock 1:1/12 to 1:1/16; hard rock almost vertical)

cut_slope_flat.source: NRS 2070 Table 11-5 Cuttings side slopes, flattest of the recommended range

bench_height.source: PLM default: NRS 2070 does not specify berms in cut slopes

bench_width.source: PLM default: NRS 2070 does not specify berms in cut slopes

max_fill_height_without_wall.source: PLM project rule (NRS 2070 cl. 17.2: retaining walls where fills on steep cross slopes are high): fills above this suggest a retaining wall

max_cut_depth_without_wall.source: PLM project rule: cuts deeper than this suggest a breast wall

drain_min_gradient.source: NRS 2070 cl. 13.8 f: side drains with at least 0.5 % longitudinal grade

drain_outlet_max_spacing.source: NRS 2070 cl. 13.8 i: outlets from side drains at no more than 500 m intervals

catch_drain_min_offset.source: NRS 2070 cl. 13.8 d: catch water drains at least 5 m behind the top of the cut

toe_drain_max_fill.source: NRS 2070 cl. 13.8 c: toe-of-slope drains in low fills below 0.8 m

design_return_period.source: NRS 2070 Table 13-2 return periods for side drain discharges

culvert_max_length.source: NRS 2070 cl. 17.1 a: cross drainage structures longer than 6 m are bridges (Nepal Bridge Standards 2067)

climbing_lane_min_width.source: NRS 2070 cl. 10.2 e: climbing lanes at least 3.5 m wide

drain_turf_min_gradient.source: NRS 2070 Table 13-3: no lining below 1 % in sandy soil and below 2 % in clayey soil; grass turfing above that

drain_hard_lining_min_gradient.source: NRS 2070 Table 13-3: stone rip-rap, masonry or concrete lining from 3 % to 5 %

subsurface_water_table_depth.source: NRS 2070 cl. 13.8 subsurface drainage a: water table kept 1.0 to 1.2 m below the subgrade
